title: About Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI

blocks.text: As organizations rapidly adopt AI capabilities embedded within everyday SaaS applications, maintaining visibility into enterprise AI usage has become increasingly challenging. Zscaler AI Security expands the AI Asset Management platform to automatically discover and identify Embedded AI applications accessed across your organization.

Unlike standalone generative AI tools, Embedded AI apps are AI-powered features built directly into popular SaaS applications, ones that employees may interact with, without explicitly recognizing them as AI. From the Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI Page, security and IT teams can now understand where embedded AI is being used alongside traditional GenAI applications.
The Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Gain a complete view of your organization's AI footprint, including AI capabilities embedded within everyday SaaS applications.
Enforce policies across both standalone Gen AI and embedded AI applications from a single platform.
Identify applications with high risk scores or sensitive data violations before they become compliance issues.
Detect emerging AI adoption patterns across departments and user groups to stay ahead of shadow AI usage.
Equip security and IT teams with the context needed to make data-driven decisions about AI usage across the enterprise.

blocks.heading: About the Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI Page

blocks.text: On the Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI page (Public AI > App Inventory > Embedded AI), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Filter the report for the Last 1 Day, Last 7 Days, Last 15 Days, Last Month, or Last Quarter.
Total Apps: View the total number of Embedded AI applications that are in use in the organization.
Total Volume: View the total bytes consumed by all the applications, both upload and download.,
Search for an Embedded AI app by name.
Show or hide columns.
View a list of all the Embedded AI applications. For each application, you can view:
Name: Name of the Embedded AI App. Click the app name to view additional details.
Total Volume: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application for both embedded AI and non-embedded AI traffic.
Total Users: The total number of users.
General Information: Information such as policies applied, Zscaler Supported Services, Tags, Notes, Headquarters, Employees, year incorporated, activities supported, integrations, description, etc.
Risk Index: The number of applications in each risk index category.
The detailed information page also displays the following tabs:
Risk Attributes
Use this tab to view the risk attributes pertaining to the Embedded AI app. The risk attributes constitute the following:

Hosting Information: Details about where the AI application is hosted, including cloud provider, region, and infrastructure information. These are risk and security posture attributes used to evaluate an app or service in an inventory, including the vendor’s compliance certifications, data retention type and description, terms of service quality, MFA support, file-sharing capabilities, data residency countries and any third-party data residency vendors, history of data breaches in the last three years, availability of admin audit logs, support for deletion upon request, source IP restriction controls, and password strength requirements.

Security Information: Security features and configurations of the AI application, including authentication, data encryption, and compliance measures. These are security posture and exposure checks used to assess the risk of a domain or cloud app, covering TLS/SSL configuration (valid SSL certificate, certificate key size, signature algorithm strength, weak cipher support, SSL pinning, DNS CAA policy, encryption in transit), HTTP hardening (support for HTTP security headers), known vulnerability exposure (published CVEs and susceptibility to Logjam, Heartbleed, and POODLE), vendor security practices (vulnerability disclosure policy and support for a WAF), email authentication controls (domain-based message authentication such as SPF and DKIM), and additional risk indicators like malware content scanning, evasive behavior, and features such as remote access/screen sharing that can increase data-exposure risk.
Users
Use this tab to view the details pertaining to the user who accessed the Embedded AI app as follows:
Search for a specific user.
Apply filters to view specific data.
View a list of users that were discovered. For each user you can view:
User Name: The name of the user associated with the AI asset app activity or record
Total Volume: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application
Upload Volume: The total bytes uploaded by the application.
Download Volume: The total bytes downloaded by the application.
Department: The name of the department the user belongs to.
No. of Transactions: The total number of transactions by the user.
Last Accessed: The timestamp of when the application was last accessed.
Locations
Use this tab to view the details pertaining to the location from where the Embedded AI app was accessed as follows:
Search for a specific location.
Apply filters to view specific data.
View a list of locations that were discovered. For each location you can view:
Location Name: The name of the location.
Total Volume: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application
Upload Volume: The total bytes uploaded by the application.
Download Volume: The total bytes downloaded by the application.
Department: The name of the department the user belongs to.
No. of Transactions: The total number of transactions by location.
Last Accessed: The timestamp of when the app was last accessed at the location.
Risk Index: The risk index number.
Total Volume: The sum of upload and download bytes of the application for both embedded and non-embedded AI traffic.
